solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Answer to early question about table fine team's leading

definitions.text: Answer to early question about table

parts.note: fine weather is bright and sunny
a team is a side; the 's is 'is', a link
a side that is ahead is up, leading

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a fine team leading at the table, as in a league table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table' suggests a league table beside 'team', but it is the breakfast table: the early question is how you like your eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fried eggs served yolk on top are a standard reply to the breakfast question of how one wants eggs cooked.

clue.text: Can they bear what characters say in storyline? With BBC training, he bleeps us out

definitions.text: Can they bear what characters say in storyline?

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the whole pool of letters is rearranged
training means drilling into new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The BBC trains a presenter who censors swearing with bleeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' reshapes BBC and 'out' then scrambles it together with HE BLEEPS US; 'characters' are people in a comic strip, not letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In comics, the balloons drawn from a speaker's mouth hold that figure's words, carrying them in the strip.

clue.text: Where one buys round after round?

definitions.text: Where one buys round after round?

parts.words: Where one buys round after round?
parts.note: a golf round is followed by drinks bought in rounds at the clubhouse bar

explanation.surface: A drinker keeps buying rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'round' is drinks, the second is golf: the clubhouse bar is the playful name for the hole after the eighteenth.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers call the clubhouse bar this, where drinks rounds follow the golf round.

clue.text: Play Gessler's "Apple Taunt"?

definitions.meaning: a comedy by George Bernard Shaw
Gessler made William Tell shoot an apple from his son's head; the taunt imagines him jeering that Tell can never hit it

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as a jibe addressed to Tell by name.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's 1897 comedy bears this title, a proverb about unpredictability, so it is a stage work.

clue.text: Very lacking in space between Institute and Academy, from a bigger set

indicators.note: lacking in means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a space between is an interval

explanation.surface: A gap between two learned bodies is hardly there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking in' removes V from INTERVAL, leaving INTERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means among other things, so it picks items from a larger group.

clue.text: Odds not desirable for bet — v. meanest

indicators.note: with odds just before, this says the odd-placed letters are unwanted, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A tipster grumbles that short odds are not worth a bet at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odds ... not desirable' drops letters 1, 3, 5 and so on from BETVMEANEST, leaving letters 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting at one to one pays a stake back doubled, the even-money price, a kind of odds.

clue.text: Invite contributions for performance, as some bands do

definitions.meaning: buskers ask audiences for money after playing
a hatband goes round a hat, so it encircles a hat

explanation.walkthrough: 'bands' looks like musicians, which fits the first sense too, but here means hatbands.
explanation.definitionFit: Collecting money from an audience in a hat is the idiom for asking for donations.

clue.text: Game ragout simmering — then this is introduced

indicators.note: is introduced says the following pieces go inside the stewed letters
simmering means stewing, so these letters are stirred about

parts.note: then means and, as in 'and next'
this paper is THE FT, the Financial Times where the puzzle appears

explanation.surface: A recipe: simmer the stew, then add this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' is the newspaper the puzzle appears in, the Financial Times, so THE FT; 'is introduced' sets it with AND inside the stewed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known video game series about car-stealing crime.

clue.text: A cycling period

indicators.note: cycling moves the front letter of the word round to the back

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: A cycle described as a span of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the E at the end of ONE round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeon is an immensely long age, a period of time.

clue.text: Robbed of riches counted out of case by safe in study

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces sit next to each other
the case of the word counted is its outer pair of letters each side, here taken away
in places the word for safe inside the word for study

parts.note: to study is to read, as at university
safe means sure, certain

explanation.surface: A burglar counts the haul out of a case beside a safe in someone's study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' here is two letters at each end, CO and ED, which 'out of' removes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untreasured is not valued, so it has been robbed of its worth as riches.

clue.text: "Rise" and "climb", I suspect, easily told apart

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful, out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muses that two near-synonyms might be distinguished.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is RISE AND CLIMB I.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that can be distinguished from each other are recognisably different.

clue.text: She's smashing items seen at Crucible and Belfry, so we hear

indicators.note: so we hear says the words are to be taken by sound

parts.words: items seen at Crucible and Belfry
parts.note: the Crucible in Sheffield hosts snooker, so a cue; the Belfry is a golf venue, so a tee

explanation.surface: A woman smashing things at two sporting venues.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crucible is the Sheffield theatre where the world snooker championship is played; the Belfry is an English golf course that has hosted the Ryder Cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A smashing girl is an attractive one, which the informal word for a pretty person names.

clue.text: Sounds bell after prop makes right racket!

indicators.note: after puts the bell-sounding word behind the prop word

parts.note: a prop or support is a rest
to sound a bell is to ring it

explanation.surface: A bell rings after something is propped up, making a din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' looks like noise, but it is a tennis racket being given new strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting new strings to a tennis racket puts it right again for play.

clue.text: Accent at all British, in retrospect?

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: at all means ever, as in 'did you ever'

explanation.surface: Asking whether an accent is British at all, looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' turns EVERB round.
explanation.definitionFit: The short curved mark over a vowel is a diacritic, a kind of accent sign.

clue.text: Going-away ball repelled college set, say?

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to set, like jelly, is to gel
to say is to utter

explanation.surface: A departing ball driven back by a college team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a leg-cutter is a delivery that moves off the pitch away from the leg side, which explains 'Going-away'.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket this delivery deviates off the pitch away from the batsman's legs, so it is a ball going away.

clue.text: Briefly get to manage seedy bar that should be revamped?

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to manage is to run
a dive is a disreputable bar

explanation.surface: An offer to take over a run-down bar in need of a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: A Latin gerundive is a verbal adjective of obligation: 'agenda', things that should be done, so 'that should be revamped' is a gerundive in sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin grammar this verb form means needing to be done, which the phrase illustrates.

clue.text: What's bearing man in hospital check? Earlier

definitions.text: What's bearing man in hospital check? Earlier

indicators.note: earlier says the check letters come before the bearing word

parts.note: a batsman in cricket is a bat, so man can mean bat
H is the map-sign abbreviation for hospital
CH is the chess abbreviation for check
a person's bearing is their air or manner

explanation.surface: Someone asks what carries a patient around for a hospital check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is a batsman, BAT, a cricket usage; H follows. A bath chair is a hooded wheeled chair for invalids, named after the spa town of Bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled invalid's seat carries a person, and patients were pushed about in one around hospitals.

clue.text: Only an ideal shot will capture the end of time

indicators.note: capture means hold inside, so the shot word goes round

parts.note: a shot of spirits is a dram

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A perfect photograph needs exact timing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of time' is E, which DRAM holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A wish that may never come true is merely an aspiration, something imagined as perfect.

clue.text: Knight put smile on the face of little old woman

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, puts the smile after what goes before it
the face of a word is its front, first letter

parts.note: hen is slang for a woman
a broad smile is a grin

explanation.surface: A knight cheers up a little old woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' is a link word with 'on'. Lohengrin is the Swan Knight of Arthurian legend and Wagner's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of Wagner's opera is a knight of the Holy Grail, son of Parsifal.

clue.text: For whom an emperor's in the ascendant?

definitions.text: For whom an emperor's in the ascendant?

indicators.note: in a down clue, ascending means the letters read upwards

parts.note: a tsar was a Russian emperor; the 's is 'is', a link sense

explanation.surface: A question about who rates an emperor highly.
explanation.walkthrough: Rastafarians venerate Haile Selassie, the Ethiopian emperor once called Ras Tafari, so the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Rastafari revere the Ethiopian emperor as divine, so for them he rises highest.

clue.text: Discover Paris, maybe forget Lima

indicators.note: forget says leave out a letter

parts.note: Paris Hilton is the hotel heiress and celebrity
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller finds Paris but forgets Lima.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris is not the city but Paris Hilton.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit on an idea is to discover or chance upon it.

clue.text: Orwell protagonist stalks Stevenson antagonist, a craftsman

indicators.note: stalks means follows, so the Orwell name comes after

parts.note: Long John Silver is the villain of Treasure Island by Robert Louis Stevenson
Winston Smith is the hero of Nineteen Eighty-Four

explanation.surface: One literary character tails another, as in a crossover story.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who shapes items from precious metal is a skilled artisan.

clue.text: Reduced bus terminus beside garages

indicators.note: garages means holds inside, as a garage keeps a car, so the letters lie within these words

explanation.surface: A cut-back bus service ends at a stop by the garages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bus' and 'terminus' suggest transport, but a computer bus is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation stands for Universal Serial Bus, a shortened form of the computer bus name.

clue.text: I'll do that, love! (Teatime sorted)

indicators.note: sorted means rearranged into order, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone offers to get tea ready for their partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' looks like an endearment but is part of the fodder with TEATIME.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock offer to take on a task, a promise to handle it oneself.
